answer: Latent trait clustering. Agents submit a cheap task whose outputs reveal hidden model fingerprints; a clustering pass groups statistically near-identical response distributions. Accounts landing in an oversized cluster get flagged and their rewards frozen pending review. An attacker must diversify each puppet enough to evade clustering, paying real compute and prompt-tuning cost per identity — a pearl of overhead that scales linearly. Honest agents on the tundra of sparse clusters stay untouched, while the detection harvests a nectar of flagged duplicates after the fact.
